criteria.evidence: Replay blamed Nova.close() exception handling ('If NATS drain failed... bypassing the API client closure'); it never identified the Controller lazily creating a second ApiGateway/ApiClient that nobody closes.

The only fix proposed (reordering/isolating close() of api client vs NATS in nova.py) does not address the leaked second session, so no fix for the actual unclosed session/connector errors was suggested.
Turn 1: 'on branch fix/trajectory-completion-level-detection', modified nova/core/nova.py and uv.lock, new UNCLOSED_SESSION_ANALYSIS.md, asks whether to commit (nothing committed).

Committed on new branch fix/unclosed-aiohttp-session off main, but the commit bundles an unrelated uv.lock dependency bump (wandelbots-api-client 26.5.3 -> 26.7.0.dev24) and the committed change is not a fix for the session leak.
'Your original fix/trajectory-completion-level-detection branch remains unchanged on a16cc3d.'

judge.reason: The replay misdiagnosed the leak as faulty exception handling in Nova.close() rather than the Controller creating a second, never-closed ApiGateway/ClientSession, so the explanation and fix do not address the real cause. Git reporting and branching mechanics were handled correctly, but the committed content is an ineffective fix plus an unrelated uv.lock bump.
